title: mail send pushes a commit with no message file and still says sent
why: A message that is lost while the sender reads "sent" breaks the mailbox route the owner ruled for every message (page item 482).
note: Filed by triage 11:03 CST Nov 10 from the session-messaging topic session (11:07 CST, its clock). Evidence: on refs/heads/mail of shivinate7/session-mailbox, commit 587de9e ("mail ea1acdfaea67", author ssemwal-cdc, 11:00:59 CST Nov 10) has the same tree as its parent 207a2b1, and the message file for id ea1acdfaea67 is in no folder, open or done. So the login and the push worked from the owner's computer, but the send lost its file. Origin: the owner's card "Test mailbox login on this computer" sent one inform to cloud/session_013NEJL1YBVqsXRPBac7nRcz. Unknown: which computer (Mac or Windows), what it printed, and whether it printed "sent". First guess, unmeasured: a path or index problem in hooks/mail.py on that OS. Done when: the cause is found, a red test shows it, and a fix lands; a send that writes no file prints "not sent", never "sent". Freeze: a fix of an item on main (#2484 session mailbox, merged in batch 71) may run; the coordinator decides. Measured on Windows (session-messaging topic session, 11:12 CST Nov 10; the owner pasted it from his card session). The PC runs Windows 11 Enterprise, hostname ssem-dpromax16. gh holds two accounts: shivinate7 is active and git uses it; the git author is ssemwal-cdc. ls-remote of the mailbox with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 exited 0 in 1.1 s with no prompt and printed refs/heads/mail at 207a2b16ee33, so Windows login works. `mail send --kind inform` exited 0 and printed "sent ea1acdfaea67", but its commit 587de9e has the same tree as its parent, so the message was lost. First guess, unmeasured: hooks/mail.py commit_tree feeds update-index --index-info text through must(..., input_text=...), and on Windows "\n" may become "\r\n" in that pipe, so git reads the path with a trailing CR. Second gap: the send never checks that the pushed tree holds the file. test_mail.py runs only in the Linux CI job (PR #1371), so no Windows case guards this. Done check: a Windows test reads the pushed tree back, and `mail send` prints "not sent" when the file is missing. The topic session calls this step mailbox-send-empty-commit. Doing 11:05 CST Nov 10: lane mail-send-no-file, session_013NEJL4CWtoG1Y8eVLppjpF (coordinator; a fix of #2484 on main, allowed under the freeze).
